intro: Old injuries and niggles, ranked by the owner (14 Nov 2026). Each has its own tests, logged over time, and its own drills. Drills marked Smith come from his course; the rest are standard physio practice (ours). Nothing here is a diagnosis: the physio confirms what each one is.

items.name: Calves: deep tenderness
items.area: Both calves, top to bottom, deep in the muscle
items.summary: Lifelong deep pain when pressed (thumbs, massage), no pain day to day. Childhood night cramps, none for years. Toe-biased movement (runs stairs on the forefoot), so the calves rarely work in their fully lengthened range.
items.likely: Tight, high-tone calves sensitised to pressure, short from habitually working in mid to short range. The toe flexors start deep in the calf, so the feet and the tucked-toe kneel are probably part of the same chain.
items.goal: Lower pressure tenderness and more ankle range: heavy, slow, full-range strength plus long-hold stretching.
items.progression: Bodyweight for the first 2-3 weeks, then add load: the Achilles adapts more slowly than the muscle.

tests.name: Knee to wall (ankle range)
tests.cue: Measured in Mobility (Squat pillar): shin angle from the clip, plus toe-to-wall distance. Around 10 cm or 35-45 deg is typical.

tests.name: Calf pressure tenderness
tests.cue: Seated, calf relaxed. Thumb into the middle of the calf belly, same spot, firm steady pressure for 5 s. Score 0 (nothing) to 10 (worst). Same spot every week.

drills.name: Slow calf raise off a step (straight knee)
drills.dose: 3 x 8-15, 3 s down, 2 s pause in the full stretch at the bottom, up under control
cues: Heel all the way below the step
Single leg once both legs are easy
Add a dumbbell after 2-3 weeks

drills.name: Seated calf raise (soleus)
drills.dose: 3 x 8-15, same slow tempo, pause at the bottom
cues: Machine, or a barbell or dumbbells on the knees (towel padding)
Balls of the feet on a platform, sink the heels

drills.name: Single-leg calf stretch off a step, three angles
drills.dose: 60-90 s per angle: forward, turned in, turned out
cues: Hold a rail, lower the heel, actively pull the foot up
Wear shoes
Which angle bites most changes: cycle all three

drills.name: Bent-knee wall calf stretch (soleus)
cues: Back knee bent, heel down, sink the knee forward

drills.name: Gentle sustained pressure (not thumbs)
drills.dose: 30-60 s per spot at about 4/10, a few spots per calf
cues: Rest the calf on a soft ball or roller and let the leg's weight sink in
Never smash: hard pressure makes it more sensitive

tips: Heat first: steam room, sauna or a hot shower on the calves before stretching
Walk heel to toe on purpose, stairs included, but keep running up stairs: it is good explosive work
red_flags: Calves ache when walking and ease when you stop
Toes or feet go white or blue in the cold
A swollen, hot or red calf
physio_questions: Assess ankle range and how I walk
GP: foot pulses (family history of poor circulation; Lp(a) and homocysteine high in April 2026); next bloods: magnesium, CK, calcium

items.name: Right foot lift: weakness after the nerve injury
items.area: Front of the right ankle and top of the foot (tibialis anterior and the toe extensors)
items.summary: Old crush injury to the nerve behind the right knee: the foot could not lift for about 6 weeks. Recovered for daily life, but the right tires much faster holding the foot up, cramps slightly on release, and the 'pop' (the tendons springing back on release from full dorsiflexion) was missing on the right until the muscle had been warmed up by tensing. Not getting weaker.
items.likely: The nerve has healed; the muscle was never trained fully back, so endurance and clean on-off control lag. Matters long term for toe clearance and balance (falls).
items.goal: Right side matches the left on the hold test, and the pop is there from cold.
items.progression: Train the right harder (an extra set) until it matches the left; the left is the benchmark.

tests.name: Foot-lift hold to fatigue
tests.cue: Seated, legs straight. Pull the foot up as far as it goes and hold. Stop when it drops or burns out. Seconds.

tests.name: The pop from cold
tests.cue: Before any warm-up: pull the right foot fully up, then release quickly. Do you feel the pop at the front?

drills.name: Tibialis raises with a band
drills.dose: 3 x 12-15 each side, 2 s squeeze at the top; right side 1 extra set
cues: Band round a post and the ball of the foot
Small range: the work is the fully shortened top position

drills.name: Wall tib raises
cues: Back against a wall, heels 20-30 cm out
Lift the toes as high as they go, lower slowly

drills.name: Foot-lift holds
cues: Seated, pull the foot up hard and hold
This is the endurance gap you felt

drills.name: Fast toe taps
cues: Seated, heel down, tap the forefoot as fast as you can

drills.name: Single-leg balance, right
drills.dose: 3 x 30 s; eyes closed once easy
cues: Barefoot, soft knee
Later: hops

red_flags: Numbness on the top of the foot or between the first two toes

items.name: Right shoulder: twinge under the side delt
items.area: Deep under the middle of the right side deltoid
items.summary: 2-3 years ago: sudden severe deep throbbing pain out of nowhere, slept sitting up in a chair, strong painkillers for a few days, no lasting weakness. The physio did needling then. Now: a slight tightness on the barbell overhead press and a small twinge lifting the arm, in the same spot. Right active flexion and pec length are the worse side in the shoulder tests.
items.likely: Possibly calcific tendinitis of the supraspinatus (the old episode fits it), with the tendon still irritated or some calcium left; a subacromial pinch overhead. Not diagnosed.
items.goal: No twinge on the press, no painful arc.
items.progression: The shoulder flexibility program carries on as planned. If the twinge has not settled after 6-8 weeks of logging, ask for a scan.

tests.name: Painful arc
tests.cue: Raise the right arm slowly out to the side, thumb up, all the way overhead. Twinge between about shoulder height and just above that eases higher up?

tests.name: Overhead press twinge
tests.cue: After your pressing sets: how much did the spot bother you, 0 (nothing) to 10.

drills.name: Side-lying external rotation
cues: Towel under the elbow, elbow at the side
Rotate the forearm up, 3 s down

drills.name: Prone Y raise (lower trap)
drills.dose: 3 x 10, 2 s hold at the top
cues: Face down, thumbs up, arms in a Y
Lift from the shoulder blades, not the neck

drills.name: Scapular wall slides
cues: Forearms on the wall, slide up while the shoulder blades rotate up and wrap round

tips: The shoulder program's external rotation and trap-3 work is the same medicine
red_flags: Numbness or tingling down the arm
physio_questions: Was the old needling dry needling, or ultrasound-guided?
Is an ultrasound or X-ray worth it to check for a calcium deposit?
Neck check: does tilting the head right and looking up bring on the delt feeling?

items.name: Right knee: behind the joint
items.area: Dead centre at the back of the right knee, top of the calf
items.summary: Flared early in the week of 9 Nov 2026 after stretching; has recurred a few times over the years. Hurts sitting back on the heels and in deep knee bending; squats on Wed 11 Nov did not aggravate it. No catching, locking or giving way. Settling.
items.likely: A strained muscle or tendon behind the knee (popliteus or the top of the calf) irritated by end-range stretching; the meniscus is less likely with no mechanical symptoms.
items.goal: Kneeling on the heels comfortable; then mark it resolved.
items.progression: Squats are fine. Ease off deep PASSIVE knee bending on the right until kneeling is comfortable.
items.caution: Right knee settling: ease off deep passive knee bending on the right (sitting back on the heels, couch stretch, deep squat holds). Squats are fine.

tests.name: Kneeling sit-back discomfort
tests.cue: Kneel and sit back towards the heels as far as is comfortable. Discomfort behind the knee, 0 (none) to 10.

drills.name: Heel digs (hamstring isometric)
cues: Seated, knee slightly bent, dig the heel into the floor

drills.name: Bodyweight squats to a comfortable depth
cues: Stop short of any pain behind the knee

red_flags: Tightness or swelling spreading down the calf
It flares every time you stretch
physio_questions: If it recurs: check the popliteus and the back of the meniscus

items.name: Feet and toes: sole tenderness
items.area: The middle of both soles; the toes
items.summary: Soles very sore under thumb pressure, fine day to day (mostly barefoot, otherwise flat shoes). Kneeling on tucked toes is very painful; kneeling with the feet flat is fine.
items.likely: Same chain as the calves: plantar fascia, the small foot muscles and the long toe flexors that start in the calf. Short and sensitised.
items.goal: Kneel on tucked toes comfortably for 60 s; lower sole tenderness.
items.progression: Hands take most of the weight at first, adding a little each week. While the right knee settles, a cushion between the heels and bum.

tests.name: Tucked-toe kneel
tests.cue: Kneel with the toes tucked under, sitting back with full weight. Seconds until you have to come off.

tests.name: Sole pressure tenderness
tests.cue: Thumb into the middle of the sole, same spot, firm 5 s. 0 (nothing) to 10.

drills.name: Tucked-toe kneel, hands supporting
cues: Hands on the floor take the weight you need
Cushion between heels and bum while the right knee settles

drills.name: Toe control (big toe up, others down, then swap)
cues: Barefoot, seated or standing

drills.name: Short foot holds
cues: Shorten the foot by lifting the arch, toes stay long and relaxed

drills.name: Gentle ball under the sole
cues: Standing, let some weight sink in, slow

tips: The calf work covers the rest of this chain
red_flags: Sharp heel pain on the first steps in the morning
Numbness or burning in the soles
